rows.q: explain alarm OVN-D02
rows.answer:
OVN-D02: oven door, Ofenschieber and lamp: I6 not reached in time.

**What the documents say** (quoted - no model was free to write this up):

#### door

Code | Alarm | Cause | Reaction | Recovery: Code OVN-D02, Alarm oven door, Ofenschieber and lamp: I6 not reached in time, Cause I6 oven feeder inside: the drive did not arrive, or the switch/barrier failed, Reaction the unit drops its outputs and goes to FAULT; no new job is given to it; the other units finish their current step and hold, Recovery clear the cause; acknowledge on the HMI; the unit re-homes, and the job restarts from its first step (the place records say where the cookie is) [PLC alarms > door]

#### Faults and wear

Alarms OVN-D (door and tray), OVN-S (gripper), OVN-T (turntable, saw, pusher), OVN-B01 (belt). Wear watched: door cylinder, gripper lowering cylinder and pusher cylinder (reed-to-reed travel time). [Machine: Oven (multi-processing station with kiln, ft 536632) > Faults and wear]

#### Faults

Id | Fault | Alarm: Id F1, Fault stuck switch, Alarm HBW-C01; Id F2, Fault motor stall, Alarm VGR-A04; Id F3, Fault cylinder never arrives, Alarm OVN-D01; Id F4, Fault lost vacuum, Alarm VGR-V01; Id F5, Fault air pressure drop, Alarm SYS-05; Id F6, Fault lost bus node, Alarm SYS-04; Id F7, Fault E-stop, Alarm SYS-01 [Panel: Commissioning > Faults]

#### In brief

Code | Meaning: Code OVN-D01 - D04, Meaning oven door and tray: I10, I6, I11, I7 not reached in time; Code OVN-S01 - S04, Meaning oven gripper: I13, I5, I8, I12 not reached in time; Code OVN-T01 - T05, Meaning turntable, saw, pusher: I15, I1, I4, I2, I14 not reached in time; Code OVN-B01, Meaning oven belt: I3 not reached in time; Code SRT-L01 - L03, Meaning sorting line: I3 not reached / pulse count not reached / bay barrier not broken; Code SYS-01, Meaning E-stop pressed (ES1, ES2 or ES3); Code SYS-02, Meaning guard door open (SA, SB or SC); Code SYS-03, Meaning safety relay feedback fault (EDM); Code SYS-04, Meaning remote I/O node lost (Modbus TCP watchdog); Code SYS-05, Meaning air pressure low at the air station [Alarm codes > In brief]

rows.q: why did the line stop this month?
rows.answer:
In the simulated two months (61 days) the line stopped 51 times (2.81 h unplanned). The biggest cause was VGR-V01 (41 stops, 136 min). Preventive maintenance caught 2 failures before they happened: VGR swivel gearbox (sudden-onset wear) (warned at hour 999, renewed at 1000, would have failed at 1091); HBW travel spindle + nut (warned at hour 225, renewed at 232, would have failed at 375).

**What the documents say** (quoted - no model was free to write this up):

#### The factory's data

Table | Rows | From: Table orders, Rows one per 12-cookie order: time, shift, duration, cookies baked, good, scrap, the QC test's fault, the hall's temperature, From the simulated month (month/orders.csv), and each order line a guest's twin finishes (source = twin, owner = the guest); Table events, Rows faults, warnings, work orders, maintenance, failures, From the month (month/events.csv); Table sensorreadings, Rows every wear part's signal, smoothed signal, health index and remaining life, per order, From the month (month/sensors.csv), condition monitoring; Table signals, Rows the hall, the colour sensor's three readings, the crane's current, the compressor's duty, per order, From the month (month/raw.csv); Table dailykpis, Rows the month day by day: orders, cookies, stops, availability, performance, quality, OEE, From the month (month/daily.csv); Table energy15min, Rows load, PV, grid [DATABASE > Guest sessions and the database > The factory's data]

#### 6. Two months of production

Both were renewed in the night gap, so no production was lost. Without the two saves shows the same two months had they been missed: 2 failures, 13.5 h of unplanned stop, 42 fewer orders. - Health shows every part's health index; move Machine age to see it wear, and switch PM off to run it until it fails. - Maintenance turns the warnings into a service plan, with the AI's predictions beside it. [User guide > 6. Two months of production]

#### The counterfactual month

The same month without preventive maintenance: what failed and what it cost. [Dashboard: Month > Sections > The counterfactual month]

#### The flow

Everything the cookie touches lies on one flow line: 1. The robot lays the raw cookie on the extended tray (Ofenschieber); light barrier I9 sees it. 2. The door opens, the tray retracts into the chamber (stop I6), the door closes. 3. Bake: the heating elements run (output Q9) until the cookie is done. 4. The door opens, the tray extends (stop I7). 5. The oven's own suction gripper (Sauger) lifts the cookie onto the turntable (Drehtisch). 6. The turntable stops under the saw, then turns to the belt; the pusher (Auswerfer, Q14) pushes the cookie onto the outlet belt. 7. The belt carries it through I3 onto the sorting line. One pneumatic stroke of the gripper (Q12) serves both the tray and the turntable, because the tray top, the turntable top and the belt top are all at the [Machine: Oven (multi-processing station with kiln, ft 536632) > The flow]

rows.q: what is the OEE?
rows.answer: OEE is 30.8 % in a shift that injects every fault once; the largest loss is performance (48.8 %). A 12-cookie order takes 429.8 s; the bottleneck is the crane (209.8 s busy of 429.8 s).

rows.q: how does the oven heat the cookies?
rows.answer:
With a real bake (about 10 min at 180 C) the oven makes 5.5 cookies an hour against 76.1 with the 2 s lamp. A fixed timer gets 79.6 % of cookies right; + dough sensors gets 99.1 %.

**What the documents say** (quoted - no model was free to write this up):

#### How to read it

1. The headline figures: cookies right first time with the best way of ending a bake, cookies an hour with a real bake, the heat per cookie. 2. One cookie in the oven: the centre waits near 100 °C while the water boils off; the colour comes last and fast. 3. Four ways to end a bake, run over the same shifts: compare how many cookies come out right, and which dough each one gets wrong. [Dashboard: Oven process > How to read it]

#### Where the heat goes

One shift's heat: walls, door, vent, the open mouth, the tray outside and the steam. [Dashboard: Oven process > Sections > Where the heat goes]

#### The bake as a process

Until step 19 the oven waited a fixed time and every cookie came out right. A real bake is heat and water: the elements heat the chamber, every door opening cools it, the cookie's surface dries and browns while its centre is still heating, and how a cookie turns out depends on the oven's state when it went in, on the dough, and on when the bake is ended. This chapter is the model of that process, built from the oven's own parts and the order's real door openings, and what it says about quality, capacity and energy. Everything is simulated; every material value is assumed and listed below, and two constants are calibrated so a nominal cookie bakes as cookies of its size do. Replace them with one measured bake before trusting the numbers. [The bake as a process]

#### The oven heating up

From switch-on to 180 °C: the elements, the air, the thermocouple and the walls, and the heater's duty. [Dashboard: Oven process > Sections > The oven heating up]

**What the documents say** (quoted - no model was free to write this up):

#### 7. The pages, in one line each

Every page has a Guide button (what it shows and the terms it uses) and an Ask button (the copilot, about that page). Captions show one line; click one to read it all. [User guide > 7. The pages, in one line each]

#### 5 Change detection

On the filter's standardised innovations, which are $N(0, 1)$ while the model holds: - CUSUM (Page): $S_t = \max(0, S_{t-1} + e_t - k)$, alarm at $S_t > h$ ($k = 0.5$, $h = 5$) - a part wearing faster than its model: a disturbance, the earliest cue to its root cause. - Bayesian online change-point detection (Adams & MacKay): the posterior of the run length since the last change - when that faster wear began. - Hotelling's $T^2$ across all ten parts against its $\chi^2_{10}$ limit - behaviour no single part's model explains (a new fault mode, a sensor gone wrong). [Predictive maintenance: the pre-failure window > The pipeline > 5 Change detection]

#### 7. The pages, in one line each

Page | Answers: Page Energy & grid, Answers The microgrid: PV, battery, peak cap, outages; Page Carbon per cookie, Answers Grams of CO₂ per cookie, and what cuts it; Page OT security / Defence in depth, Answers The network, the threats and the controls; Page Engineering / Validation / Data, Answers How the twin is built and checked [User guide > 7.
